QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_21

question.text: A client has a gross open position in USDINR futures with a mark-to-market notional value of Rs 36 crore. The Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) rate for USDINR futures per the Currency Derivatives workbook is 0.50% of the mark-to-market value of gross open positions. What is the ELM amount the clearing corporation will levy?

answer.text: Rs 18 lakh — 0.50% of Rs 36 crore MTM notional
Rs 36 lakh, because ELM is 1.00% for USDINR futures
Rs 72 lakh, because ELM is 2% for currency derivatives similar to equity index futures
Rs 1.26 crore, because ELM is 3.5% for all exchange-traded derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: The Currency Derivatives workbook states that the ELM for USDINR futures is 0.50% of the mark-to-market value of the gross open position. ELM = 0.50% × Rs 36,00,00,000 = Rs 18,00,000 = Rs 18 lakh. The Trap: A 1.00% rate is not what the workbook specifies for USDINR futures. The 2% and 3.5% figures are equity-segment ELM rates for index and stock derivatives respectively and do not apply here. Note: ELM is levied over and above SPAN margin. It is computed on the MTM value of gross open positions rather than on raw USD notional, so any rupee figure depends on the prevailing USDINR rate used to mark the position.
